body: Read the existing structured research brief, preserving original requirements, reused research, essential_questions, limitations, unavailable_evidence and more_research. This stage classifies clarification need only: do not answer essential questions, perform research, approve engineering or create CAD. Inspect essential_questions entries containing question, consequence and resolution. If any consequential essential question requires declared_user_input, return exactly {"version":"wright.requirements-resolution/1","unresolved_fields":["clarification"],"resolved_values":{}} through the existing response envelope. Otherwise return exactly {"version":"wright.requirements-resolution/1","unresolved_fields":[],"resolved_values":{"clarification":"No user clarification required by this research brief."}}. The latter value is an explicit skip marker, never a simulated human answer. Questions assigned targeted_research remain research matters; do not answer them or reassign them to the user merely because a research provider is unavailable. Provider absence remains a limitation, not an approval request. If the upstream brief is malformed or inaccessible, use the existing blocked/error outcome with a diagnostic; do not infer that no questions exist. Do not repeat dynamic question text: the human receives the original brief and resolution. Use only the existing validated conditional human-input contract; introduce no routing implementation or prompt-based branch.
